question.text: Ammonia forms the complex ion $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\right]^{2+}$ with copper ions in alkaline solutions but not in acidic solutions. What is the reason for it?

options.text: In acidic solutions protons coordinate with ammonia molecules forming $\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}$ions and $\mathrm{NH}_3$ molecules are not available
In alkaline solutions insoluble $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{OH})_2$ is precipitated which is soluble in excess of any alkali
Copper hydroxide is an amphoteric substance
In acidic solutions hydration protects copper ions.
